terms.gloss: the connection, the run of a text; context
evidence: Cic. Part. 82: in tōtō quasi contextū ōrātiōnis
M-O s.v. circumstance: context (verbōrum contextus)
terms.comment: A joining together: the coherence of a speech or a system (Cic. Fin. 5.83), the run of the words (very frequent in Quintilian). Cicero softens it with quasi. It is not the circumstances of an event, which Latin calls rēs or tempora.

terms.gloss: what is written before and after (a passage)
terms.comment: Cicero’s way of saying that the context settles an ambiguous word.

phrases.latin: deinde ex superiōre et ex īnferiōre scrīptūrā docendum id, quod quaerātur, fierī perspicuum.
phrases.english: next, one must show from what is written before and after that the point in question becomes clear.

phrases.latin: sed in tōtō quasi contextū ōrātiōnis haec erunt inlūstranda maximē
phrases.english: but in the whole fabric, so to speak, of the speech these points will have to be brought out most of all
